summary: Declare metric thresholds in KDL; the daemon evaluates conditions in the background and notifies owners once on breach and recovery.

replay.detail: No graph replay; one-time re-admission of old unknown-family invalid records per new schema digest. Local condition heads re-seed through bounded indexed seeks whenever declarations change.

schema.detail: Adds condition declarations and condition-instance/condition-hash/origin-hash/instance-hash subjects with authenticated system-only durable transitions. Storage version stays 18; four local cache tables and a desired-condition partial index are created on open, without a global claims-index build.

rules.detail: condition.state is durable and never trimmed: no checkpoint rule changes. Only entry/recovery append; routine and hold phases stay local. At minimum holds plus cooldown, flapping can append about two claims per seven minutes (~411/day/instance), at most 32 declarations x eight local instances. This is a worst-case transition bound, not a steady-sample stream.

compatibility.detail: Adds /v1/conditions and st conditions ls/show. Client-v0 adds condition attention kind; generated clients/digest change and stui renders these alerts. Deploy all daemons before facts, daemon before CLI, and clients before person-owned declarations. Old daemons mark condition intent.desired invalid (degraded envelope) and condition.state unknown; these heal once after upgrade without replication repair.

downtime.detail: Ordinary daemon restart; breaches resume silently, holds restart. Evaluation and live file+WAL size sampling every 30 seconds; one disk worker with stale diagnostics. Physical daily growth is deferred to the shared SLO sampler adapter; no separate hourly ring.

manual.detail: Operations must deploy all fleet daemons before publishing the first conditions. Keep existing watches until real-host breach/recovery verification and operations approval. Publication caps subtract same-apply stops; out-of-band replicated over-cap declarations produce an explicit invalid-declaration diagnostic. Missing breached instances remain last-known breach until measured recovery; absence cannot prove recovery. Process PID enumeration is bounded and may miss processes beyond the cap. Background tasks stop when the daemon runtime shuts down; an uninterruptible kernel call may delay shutdown.

recovery.detail: Roll forward after declarations exist. An older daemon cannot evaluate them. Unknown-family records rejected by old registries heal on an upgraded schema; other invalid records require normal replication repair. Durable notification retries are idempotent, limited to three failures per row, and visible in doctor.
